result.title: BEACON: Learning Observation-Conditioned Starting Points for Guided Conditional Flow Matching in Microscopy
result.comment: 30 pages, 25 figures, 2 tables; main paper (10 pages) followed by supplementary material
result.summary: Fluorescence microscopy drives much of modern life science, but accessible imaging setups often yield images degraded by out-of-focus light, limited resolution, and strong signal-dependent noise. Computational restoration can recover high-quality images from such data, enabling cheaper and faster imaging at lower light dose, provided biologically meaningful structures are preserved. Guided conditional flow matching has recently shown strong results for microscopy dehazing and computational super-resolution by learning distributions of plausible restorations. However, it pairs each clean target with an independent standard Gaussian sample, so the starting point of every training path does not leverage the degraded observation. This arbitrary noise--target coupling can produce conflicting velocity targets and makes the conditional velocity field harder to learn. We present BEACON, a $BE$st-of-$K$ $A$daptive learned coupling for guided $CON$ditional flow matching, which learns an observation-conditioned base distribution. During training, a lightweight conditional noise model proposes $K$ starting points for each degraded input, and the candidate with the lowest flow-matching loss supervises both networks, while a KL term keeps the proposal close to the Gaussian prior. At inference, a single draw from the learned proposal is transported along the velocity field, requiring neither candidate selection nor the target. We evaluate BEACON on ten datasets spanning microscopy dehazing and computational super-resolution against 13 baseline families. BEACON achieves the best median perception--distortion rank for every pairing of a fidelity metric (PSNR, MicroMS-SSIM) with a perceptual metric (LPIPS, FID). Code and pretrained models will be released under a permissive license.

AI.brief_summary: 论文面向荧光显微图像去雾与计算超分辨，指出 guided conditional flow matching 将干净目标与独立高斯噪声配对会使速度场难以学习，提出 BEACON：用轻量条件噪声模型基于退化观测生成 K 个候选起点，以流动匹配损失最小的候选监督两个网络，并用 KL 项约束贴近高斯先验；推理时只需一次采样，在十个数据集上与 13 类基线比较感知—失真综合排序。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「由观测条件化的初始分布 + best-of-K 轨迹监督」线索或可供核查 LVR 中 latent 状态的初始化与轨迹训练监督选择问题，但该工作是图像复原而非多模态推理，迁移性需进一步判断。
